## CELL FACTS

Cell 水_正官 (Water carrying The Magistrate). Persona The Magistrate (正官). Definition line: "Framework-mediated pressure, the standard that steadies". Keyword Order, charge gentle, poles catalyst Integrity / friction Rigidity. Family function: Order. Cost dimension: the standard that steadies; the frame that holds you holds you in. Arena: the gate, the seal, order, the appointed hour. Classical portrait: framework-mediated pressure; the standard that steadies; rank held by rules, rigidity as the shadow. Ruled domains: Career, Status, Order. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 七杀.
Element arena: Water (depth, current, tide, rain, spring, flow). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Fire. structural_interaction seed: "Water setting standard for Fire cross-polarity — depth asking whether warmth is sustainable".
- k2_overview: "Your Water moves as the Magistrate: navigable law, order that flows. You govern the way good rivers govern valleys, setting course without shouting, adjusting to terrain while staying a river. Your rules bend around cases and still arrive at the sea. It is the subtlest authority, and people obey it thinking they chose to."
- k2_functional: "Your order runs like a canal: dug once with care, then carrying everyone’s traffic for decades."
- adj_chips: {"friction":["Overcautious","Muted","On rails"],"catalyst":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Career":"Your career advances by navigation: reading currents, timing passages, arriving at rank without visible strain. Diplomacy, coordination, the harbor-master roles. Your course is quiet and it compounds.","Status":"Your standing spreads like watershed reputation: carried by word of mouth into places you have never been. Tend the source. Everything downstream tastes of it.","Order":"Your order is current-shaped: rules that adapt to terrain yet keep direction. People experience your governance as ease. Document the channel, or it evaporates when you do."}

- Sibling cell 水_七杀 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Cool-headed","Unblinking","Deep-striking"],"friction":["Chilling","Relentless","Suffocating"]}
- Sibling cell 水_七杀 catalyst row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your temperature drops as situations heat up, which is backwards from most people and priceless in a crisis. The angrier the meeting, the clearer your sentences get. Decisions made in your coolness hold up later, when everyone rereads what the heat almost signed."

Core element Fire, energy element Water. Law: Water tames Fire (水克火: rain ends the blaze). Relative to the core the energy is the tamer, so Water is this core's Order. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Fire core that shows Water on the catalyst pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The catalyst pole of Water as the Order is the Overfueled band's case (the core has more than it channels); tone by pole: compliment. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 火_水's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: You follow through long after the mood that said yes has gone. Following through matters more to you than improving the plan, so you finish the version you announced. Let a better version in sometimes, since following through never meant never changing course.

value_b.text: Following through is your word to yourself. You would rather follow a plan made calm than chase the halfway idea, since calm is the state you trust. Keep an hour a week for it, because following through on the right thing beats finishing the first.

value.text: You earn trust slowly and prefer it that way. You care about being counted on more than being liked, so you earn trust by record rather than by charm. Let a little warmth go first sometimes, since trust earned slowly needs a reason to start.

value_b.text: Trust is something you earn slowly, on purpose. Since you would rather be sure of someone than quick with them, you earn trust in small pieces and keep each one. Give a bigger piece first sometimes, because trust earned slowly can be earned too slowly.

value.text: Trust from you is earned as slowly as you earn it. Because easy trust feels false, you make a new person earn it rather than let them in early. Offer the welcome sooner, since earning your trust slowly costs them a warmth already earned.

value.text: You pace yourself through things other people sprint. You care more about arriving without strain than arriving first, and you keep a pace you can hold for years. Speed up once in a while, since pacing yourself only counts if you arrive.

value_b.text: Pacing yourself is a daily decision. Because you would rather last than win for a season, you hold your pace and let the quick ones pass. Let yourself be passed, since the pace you keep is why you are there at the end.

value.text: Not breaking is what pacing yourself is for. Since a sprint costs the steadiness you built, you keep your pace rather than take the opening that needs a rush. Rush sometimes, because the chance that needs a sprint closes while you pace yourself toward it.

value.text: Pacing yourself paces everyone beside you. You would rather arrive together than let one run ahead, and you keep everyone at your speed. Let someone run ahead sometimes, since pacing them to you costs them a finish of their own.
